Band IV.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Band IV.question: The _____ was Radio frequency range in the UHF band.
Band IV.fact: Band IV is the name of a radio frequency range within the ultra high frequency part of the electromagnetic spectrum. For example, the Swiss Federal Office of Communications, the Broadcast engineer's reference book and Ericsson India Ltd all define the range of Band IV from 470 to 582 MHz.

Band IV.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Band IV.question: An _____ paper defines the range as 474 to 602 MHz, whilst the BBC define the range as 470 to 614 MHz
Band IV.fact: An EICTA paper defines the range as 474 to 602 MHz, whilst the BBC define the range as 470 to 614 MHz.

Band V.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Band V.question: The _____ was Radio frequency range.
Band V.fact: Band V (meaning Band 5) is the name of a radio frequency range within the ultra high frequency part of the electromagnetic spectrum. Band V is primarily used for analogue and digital (DVB-T & ATSC) television broadcasting, as well as radio microphones and services intended for mobile devices such as DVB-H. With the close-down of analog television services most countries have auctioned off frequencies from 694 MHz and up to 4G cellular network providers.

Band V.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Band V.question: The IPTV _____ define the range as 582 to 806 MHz and the DVB Worldwide website refers to the range as 585 to 806 MHz
Band V.fact: The IPTV India Forum define the range as 582 to 806 MHz and the DVB Worldwide website refers to the range as 585 to 806 MHz.

Band V.question: Rows with an orange background (channels 49–60 inclusive) indicate channels that are due to be cleared so that from _____ they can be used by mobile data services
Band V.fact: Rows with an orange background (channels 49–60 inclusive) indicate channels that are due to be cleared so that from 2022 they can be used by mobile data services.
